author: EmuCore - Hub
title: Big Picture brings PCSX2 to the living room
summary: PCSX2's controller-first fullscreen interface turns launching, configuring and resuming games into a couch-friendly workflow.
heroAlt: Big Picture brings PCSX2 to the living room
searchKeywords: Big Picture brings PCSX2 to the living room

blocks.text: Big Picture mode is built for directional navigation, large television viewing distances and gamepad confirmation rather than mouse-sized desktop controls. PCSX2 can start directly in this interface, boot a selected game fullscreen and close with the session through documented command-line options.

The fullscreen UI uses an ImGui implementation led by Stenzek instead of stretching the Qt desktop window. That choice gives the controller path its own focus, animation and layout rules while it continues to read the same game library and emulator configuration as the desktop front end.
Critical actions stay on the couch

The interface exposes game launch, properties, controller configuration, save states and other session actions needed during play. A user does not need to reach for a mouse simply because one title needs a different profile or because a previous state must be selected.

Qt remains the detailed desktop environment for logs, debugging and keyboard-heavy administration. Big Picture presents the same underlying titles and settings with controller-sized controls. Fixing metadata or changing an override in one path does not create a second, divergent library.

PCSX2 documents CLI switches for fullscreen startup, Big Picture startup and process behavior after a game exits. Front ends and living-room shortcuts can use those supported arguments instead of simulating clicks, producing a predictable handoff between a launcher and the emulator. Because focus order is designed for a controller, every important action needs a predictable path back to the library and the currently selected game. That is more than a visual theme: it prevents modal desktop dialogs from trapping a television setup, keeps confirmation targets readable at distance and allows a launcher appliance to operate without a hidden mouse or keyboard step.
